resources.string: Measure a ring, or your finger with a strip of paper, and get the size in the systems jewellers use.
Lay the ring flat on the plate. Drag on the plate until the drawn circle is exactly as wide as the inside edge of the ring.
Wrap a strip of paper round your finger and mark where it overlaps. Lay the strip on the ruler and move the line until it ends at the mark.
Certain to about %1$s of a size
Make the ruler exact first. One ring size is 1 mm apart, and a ruler that is only a guess from your screen is about three sizes out.
That circle is smaller than the smallest size the size chart publishes.
That circle is bigger than any size the size chart publishes.
This screen can only draw %1$s mm of paper, so the paper method reaches size %2$s at most. Use the ring method, or measure on a bigger screen.
Circle plate. Drag on the plate to make the drawn circle exactly as wide as the inside of your ring.
Ruler plate with a measuring line. Lay the paper strip on the screen and move the line to the mark on it.
How wide is the inside of the ring?
How long is the paper strip?

Sizes come from published size charts. An EU size is the inside circumference in millimetres, a US size counts steps of 0.8 millimetres, a UK size is a letter, and a Japanese size counts thirds of a millimetre.
